subject.title: [Bug]: `exec` tool does not inherit `skills.entries.*.env` environment variables

question: Should explicitly configured credential-shaped `skills.entries.<skill>.env` names bypass the generic sensitive-name block for active host skill execution, and what isolation rule prevents unrelated exec children from receiving those secrets?
rationale: The bug contradicts documented host-run skill env behavior, but the fix changes a credential-to-exec boundary and intersects existing protections against skill secret leakage.

options.title: Admit scoped active-skill env secrets
options.body: Permit explicitly configured keys for the intended active skill path, keep dangerous host env names blocked, and add regression coverage for unrelated exec and ACP isolation.

options.title: Keep metadata-only sensitive admission
options.body: Require skills to declare every credential-shaped env name in metadata and update docs or doctor guidance so arbitrary env credentials are not promised.

options.title: Defer to a new secret contract
options.body: Leave the sanitizer unchanged until maintainers define a SecretRef or plugin-owned credential path for CLI skills that need headless auth.

recommendation.title: Admit scoped active-skill env secrets
recommendation.body: Permit explicitly configured keys for the intended active skill path, keep dangerous host env names blocked, and add regression coverage for unrelated exec and ACP isolation.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved decision is primarily the host exec env security boundary, where this owner has the clearest merged-history signal.
